A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dist Loss study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original age-estimation and ECG potassium-prediction experiments, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, timing measurements, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds prediction-versus-label visualizations across the three datasets in Appendix A.5.1.

M1.justification: The intended procedure retains KDE-based pseudo-label generation, differentiable prediction sorting, and joint distribution-distance and sample-level losses. Equation (2) is reformulated, but the frequency-replication description and worked example remain unchanged, without evidence of an altered training algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate IMDB-WIKI-DIR, AgeDB-DIR, and the same ECG potassium dataset, including its eight imbalance-ratio variants. ECG-Ka-DIR is renamed ECG-K-DIR; the new scatter plots use existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: The corresponding quantitative comparisons retain vanilla, LDS, FDS, RankSim, ConR, and Balanced MSE, including combinations with Dist Loss. Figure 7 visualizes already-compared vanilla and LDS models without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, shot thresholds, MAE/GM metrics, architectures, training budgets, and batch-size settings remain unchanged. Removing the statement about RankSim's original-paper 120-epoch budget does not change this study's stated 90-epoch setup. The new scatter plots introduce no stated testing-protocol change.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5.1 and Figure 7 add prediction-versus-label diagnostics for vanilla, LDS, and Dist Loss across all three datasets. The loss-function and batch-size ablations, imbalance-ratio tests, and sorted-error analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. The added scatter plots display individual predictions rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–13 are unchanged, including Table 1's Dist Loss few-shot MAEs of 22.550, 9.122, and 1.329. Figure 7 adds qualitative evidence about prediction alignment and persistent ECG prediction compression, without revising benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equation (2) replaces the unit-step-based pseudo-label formula with a cumulative-frequency indexing expression. This is a localized revision to the mathematical specification; the worked example and differentiable-sorting mathematics remain unchanged, and no new proof or theorem is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain distribution alignment for imbalanced regression, state-of-the-art few-shot performance, and compatibility with existing methods. v2 emphasizes the dual objective more explicitly, but both components were already described in v1.

C2.justification: v2 explains the preference for full-distribution pseudo-labels over sorted batch labels. Appendix A.5.1 newly attributes ECG prediction difficulty to limited single-lead information and regression dilution, and interprets the scatter plots as evidence of robustness to imbalanced, noisy data.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an implementation repository link where v1 promises a future release. It also explicitly identifies the illustrated vanilla model's L1 loss and connects M to training batch size. These are documentation additions; existing hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same works, and the positioning relative to classification methods and existing imbalanced-regression approaches remains substantively unchanged. Additional introduction citations refer to works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The abstract, much of the introduction, Section 2.2, and portions of Sections 3.1–3.2 receive extensive paragraph-level rewriting. Explanations of the dual objective, discretization, KDE, and sorted sequences are expanded, alongside terminology, author-note, and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds the explanatory schematic in Figure 3 and the nine-panel prediction visualization in Figure 7, and revises Figure 2 and its caption. Existing tables and other plots retain their structure and content, with renumbering, dataset-label updates, and page reflow.

improvement.justification: Clearer method explanations, additional schematics and prediction diagnostics, and the supplied implementation link improve readability and reproducibility information. The gains are limited: numerical validation is unchanged, and existing reporting problems, including unexplained repetition of cross-dataset values in Table 9, remain.
